issue: dwóh₁ ḱwṓ ... h₂lékseti: 'two dogs' needs the nom. dual ḱwónh₁(e), not nom. sg. ḱwṓ, and the verb must be 3du h₂léksetes, not 3sg. Minor: h₁áyih₁to (mid. opt.) keeps the accented full-grade root where the root aorist should have zero grade with the accent on the ending.

deywṓs ... dʰh₁tóm: dʰh₁tóm is the aorist 2du; plural subject 'the gods set' needs 3pl dʰh₁ént. Minor: bʰúHyeh₁t puts the accent on the root; the optative should be suffix-accented bʰuHyéh₁t. It also alternates with bʰuh₂yéh₁t (a different lemma) for the same 'may X become Y' frame.
kʷíd yemHóns loykʷóm h₁ésti?: yemHóns is acc. pl. 'twins'; 'left of the twin' needs abl. yemHṓd (the answer itself uses abl. h₁ésmōd) or gen. yemHósyo.

h₁égʷʰis h₃ésth₁h₂ 'the serpent's bones': this is the engine's acrostatic gen. sg., but it looks exactly like a nominative and clashes with the nom. h₁ógʷʰis earlier in the text; h₁égʷʰeys would be clear. spért 'freed' rests on a weakly supported *sper- 'free, rescue'.

dyḗws ... kʷr̥tó. h₁íh₂ pl̥th₂éwih₂ h₁ést 'It was broad': the antecedent is masc. dyḗws, but the pronoun and adjective are feminine. Read as fem., they point to the earth (the Vedic pṛthivī́ epithet), so the PIE no longer matches the English. Masc. h₁éy pléth₂us/pl̥th₂ús is needed, or the English should say the earth.
ǵʰwḗres ḱunés bʰugént: past/injunctive 3pl for present 'flee' in a present-tense narrative. polh₁éwes (masc. pl.) for 'them' = water (n.) + wool (f.): the gender resolution is questionable.

This is a scholarly reconstruction (Byrd's 'King and God' line). The English 'to pray' renders the finite imperfect h₁yaǵeto as a purpose clause; it means '(and) now he prayed to the god'. sesole is unaccented and h₃rḗḱs is spelled phonetically (cf. h₃rḗǵs elsewhere).
bʰrés h₁nómn̥ ḱlutéh₂bʰos h₁ésti: ḱlutéh₂bʰos is fem. dat./abl. pl.; the predicate of neut. h₁nómn̥ must be nom. sg. neut. ḱlutóm.

pléth₂ewes: full-grade, root-accented nom. pl. comes from the lexicon headword pléth₂us; the handbook form is pl̥th₂éwes (Ved. pṛthávaḥ, Gk platús). It is also inconsistent with fem. pl̥th₂éwih₂ in 2e8228c6.
ǵʰiméni pr̥kʷéwi stn̥h₂ént 'they stood': the nasal present *st-n-eh₂- is transitive ('place, set up'); intransitive 'stood' wants sth₂éh₁yont or stéh₂n̥t.

bʰéwdʰt 'he wakes up', bʰudʰént 'do not wake up', léwkt 'becomes bright': aorist/injunctive forms in a gnomic present text, although thematic presents exist (bʰéwdʰeti). This is defensible as gnomic injunctive but ambiguous in tense.
Scholarly-style line from Schleicher's fable in pre-laryngeal notation (owis, aǵontm̥, eḱwons, no accents). agʰnutai has a Greek-style -tai; PIE 3sg mid. is -toy/-tor (Lehmann-Zgusta agʰnutoi).
péh₂wr̥ ... l̥h₂tós: masc. adjective on a neut. subject; needs l̥h₂tóm. wiHróns h₁ésmi sédt 'a man sat down': wiHróns is acc. pl.; needs nom. sg. wiHrós.
supnós ... gʷémt 'Sleep comes': aorist 3sg in present-tense hymn text, though the present gʷm̥yéti is used elsewhere in the corpus.

snóygʷʰōs tinéh₁ti 'the snow melts': snóygʷʰōs is nom. pl., but the verb is singular; needs nom. sg. snóygʷʰos. Also aorist/past forms (studént, kʷélh₁t, léytt, bʰwéh₂t, h₂uksént) appear in a present-tense seasonal hymn.
h₂wést, léwkt, séngʷt are aorist/injunctive forms for present 'dawns / becomes bright / sinks' in a present-tense hymn.

h₂éngʷʰis bʰṓr-kʷe ... h₁pyéh₁t: a singular verb with a conjoined subject (agreement with the nearest conjunct is possible, but plural h₁pih₁ént is expected). bʰúHih₁n̥t is root-accented, beside suffix-accented h₂uksih₁ént.

Scholarly-style Schleicher line in pre-laryngeal notation (owis, wl̥nā, eḱwons, gʷr̥um for gʷr̥h₂úm, no accents). The relative yesmin is masc./neut. loc., but its antecedent owis is feminine (fem. *yesyeh₂i expected).
